{{short description|French physicist and mathematician}}
'''Jean-Pierre Gazeau''' (born 10 October 1945) is a French physicist and mathematician who works in the field of symmetry in quantum physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Pierre Gazeau |url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/en/users/gazeau |website=Publons |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> His research has focused on [[coherent states]]; beta numeration for quasicrystals, and more generally for aperiodic order; and [[de Sitter space]] and [[anti-de Sitter space]] times. He is a professor emeritus at [[Paris Diderot University]], [[Sorbonne Paris Cité University (group)]].Through a career spanning 50 years, he has held research and teaching positions on five continents, with a particular concentration on developing and emerging countries.{{citation needed|date=September 2019}}

== Education ==
Gazeau graduated in applied mathematics from the University of Paris Faculty of Sciences in 1967.<ref>{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE JEAN-PIERRE GAZEAU |url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/sites/default/files/cvgazeaujp_1.pdf |website=Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory |publisher=Paris Diderot University |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> He earned his doctorate in science at the University Paris 6 (Pierre-et-Marie Curie) in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE JEAN-PIERRE GAZEAU |url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/sites/default/files/cvgazeaujp_1.pdf |website=Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory |publisher=Paris Diderot University |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gazeau is the author ''"Coherent States in Quantum Physics"'' (2009).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gazeau |first1=Jean-Pierre |title=Coherent states in quantum physics |date=23 September 2009 |publisher=Wiley-VCH |isbn=978-3-527-40709-5 |pages=358 |url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Coherent+States+in+Quantum+Physics-p-9783527407095 |archive-date=15 August 2019 |access-date=15 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190815162912/https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Coherent+States+in+Quantum+Physics-p-9783527407095 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is the co-author of ''"Coherent States, Wavelets and Their Generalizations"'',<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ali |first1=Syed Twareque |last2=Antoine | first2=Jean-Pierre |last3=Gazeau |first3=Jean-Pierre |title=Coherent States, Wavelets and Their Generalizations |date=2014 |publisher=Springer Verlag |location=New York |isbn=978-1-4614-8534-6 |pages=XVIII, 577 |edition=2nd |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9781461485346}}</ref> initially published in 2000 with a revised edition in 2014.At Paris Diderot University, Gazeau served as vice president for communication from 1992-1997. Under Gazeau's initiative, supported by several colleagues, the university in 1994 held an event – [[Denis Diderot]] Days – to explore the philosopher's work and impact.<ref>{{cite web |title=Université Paris Diderot : archives des journées Denis Diderot (1993-1995) |url=https://www.siv.archives-nationales.culture.gouv.fr/siv/rechercheconsultation/consultation/ir/consultationIR.action?irId=FRAN_IR_055521 |website=Online Catalogue |publisher=French Archives National |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> The theme was "The transmission of academic knowledge through the book". The events were held under the patronage of French President François Mitterrand and sponsored by the Minister of Culture and Francophonie, the Minister of Higher Education and Research, the Chancellor of Universities and the Office of Paris Mayor [[Jacques Chirac]].{{citation needed|date=September 2019}}

Gazeau is affiliated with top scientific institutions in France: the [[Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory]]; the National Centre for Space Studies [[CNES]]; the [[Paris Observatory]]; and the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|National Center of Scientific Research]]. In Brazil, he is affiliated with the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas|Brazilian Center for Research in Physics]] (CPBF).{{citation needed|date=September 2019}}

He has served as a visiting researcher in the United States, Canada, Japan and several European countries outside of France. In addition, he has served as a visiting researcher in Brazil; at [[Chern Institute of Mathematics]] at Nankai University<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gazeau (et al, eds) |first1=Jean-Pierre |title=Symmetries And Groups In Contemporary Physics – Proceedings of the XXIX International Colloquium on Group-Theoretical Methods In Physics |date=2012 |publisher=World Scientific |location=Singapore |isbn=978-981-4518-54-3 |pages=664 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MDe7CgAAQBAJ&q=%22nankai+university%22+gazeau&pg=PR3 |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> in Tianjin, China; and at the Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences in Tehran, Iran<ref>{{cite web |title=Lecture series by Prof. Jean Pierre Gazeau |url=http://physics.ipm.ac.ir/Prof.Gazeau.pdf |website=IPM - Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, School of Physics |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> He also has been a visiting professor in Algeria, Bangladesh, Benin, Burundi, Morocco and Nicaragua.<ref>{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE JEAN-PIERRE GAZEAU |url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/sites/default/files/cvgazeaujp_1.pdf |website=Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory |publisher=Paris Diderot University |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref>

=== Influential students ===
Among early-career scientists who have studied for their doctoral degrees under Gazeau, several have gone on to distinguished careers:

[[Romain Murenzi]], executive director of TWAS, He got his PhD iat the Université Catholique de Louvain-La-Neuve (Belgium) under the supervision of Jean-Pierre Antoine (for the main thesis) and Jean-Pierre Gazeau (for the second thesis)

Mathematician [[Jacques Renaud]] was appointed in 2016<ref>{{cite web |title=Jacques Renaud nommé directeur de l'Espé de Versailles |url=https://www.letudiant.fr/educpros/nominations/jacques-renaud-nomme-directeur-de-l-espe-de-versailles.html |website=EducPros |publisher=L'Etudiant |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> to a five-year term directing Espé, the Higher School of Teaching and Education of the Academy of Versailles.

[[Simon Labrunie]],<ref>{{cite web |title=La page personnelle de Simon Labrunie |url=http://www.iecl.univ-lorraine.fr/%7ESimon.Labrunie/ |publisher=Institute Élie Cartan De Lorraine |accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref> an associate professor at the University of Lorraine in France, is co-author of "Mathematical Foundations of Computational Electromagnetism" (Springer, 2018).

== Non-scientific work ==

Gazeau's niece, [[Sophie Toscan du Plantier]], was murdered in Ireland in December 1996. In 2007 the case remained unsolved, and Gazeau formed an association to focus attention on the crime and to press for continued investigation.<ref>{{cite news |title=DNA hope in hunt for Sophie's killer |url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/dna-hope-in-hunt-for-sophies-killer-26457900.html |accessdate=15 August 2019 |work=The Independent |date=28 June 2008}}</ref> Gazeau is the president of the Association for the Truth about the Murder of Sophie Toscan du Plantier née Bouniol.<ref>{{cite news |title=French group campaigning for justice for Sophie Toscan du Plantier criticise Irish authorities |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/crime-and-law/french-group-campaigning-for-justice-for-sophie-toscan-du-plantier-criticise-irish-authorities-1.1523364 |accessdate=15 August 2019 |publisher=The Irish Times |date=11 September 2013}}</ref> British journalist Ian Bailey was arrested twice in relation to the murder, but maintained his innocence. On 31 May 2019 Bailey was convicted of murder in absentia by the Cour d'Assises de Paris and sentenced to 25 years in prison.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris court finds Briton Ian Bailey guilty in Sophie Toscan du Plantier murder case |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2019/05/31/paris-court-hands-briton-25-year-sentence-murder-frenchwoman/ |accessdate=15 August 2019 |publisher=The Telegraph |date=31 May 2019}}</ref> Based on the verdict, France is seeking to extradite him from Ireland. In June 2019, the French court ordered Bailey to pay €115,000 to reimburse the French agency that compensated the victim's family.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sophie Toscan du Plantier murder: Ian Bailey told to pay €115,000 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48620784 |accessdate=15 August 2019 |publisher=BBC News |date=13 June 2019}}</ref>
